j-oop-01-q1: How does U2 affect an already assigned A1? => The call returns false and U1 remains owner.
j-oop-01-q2: Where should duplicate-ID detection keep membership history? => In a set built as the input is scanned.
j-oop-01-q3: A1 starts free. U1 successfully claims it. U2 then makes a valid claim. Which observations best establish the invariant? => U1 succeeds, U2 conflicts, final owner is U1.
j-oop-01-q4: A browser shows A1 as available but POST /bookings returns 409. Which state is authoritative? => The result of the enforcing booking operation
j-oop-01-q5: Which operation is appropriate for the LLM in this project? => Draft a help answer checked against policy evidence
j-concurrency-01-q1: Can two check-then-act calls both read an unowned seat? => Yes, if both reads occur before either write.
j-concurrency-01-q2: What makes the race reproducible? => Synchronize the test at the decisive interleaving boundary.
j-concurrency-01-q3: In the unsafe fixture both workers read null before either writes. Their methods return true and one owner remains. What happened? => Both callers raced through the check and one write overwrote the other.
j-concurrency-01-q4: Two threads share one Seat. Thread T1 runs claim("U1") and T2 runs claim("U2") with no synchronization. Which outcome is NOT possible? => T1 false, T2 false, owner null
j-concurrency-01-q5: Which variables are shared between two threads that call seat.claim(user) on the same object? => The instance field owner
j-concurrency-02-q1: What does volatile alone provide here? => Visibility and ordering for that field, with a possible race across the sequence.
j-concurrency-02-q2: What makes synchronized coordinate both requests? => They acquire the same monitor around the entire decision.
j-concurrency-02-q3: A service locks its own instance during claim. Two service instances share the same Seat. Which change coordinates those callers inside one JVM? => Guard every check and write with the same monitor on the shared seat.
j-concurrency-02-q4: The booking service runs as two instances behind a load balancer, each with synchronized claim on its own Seat object. What prevents double booking? => An atomic conditional update in the shared database, such as UPDATE … WHERE owner IS NULL
j-equality-01-q1: What must hold for equal keys? => They have equal hash codes.
j-equality-01-q2: When is constant HashMap lookup a useful claim? => As an expected bound with suitable hash distribution and key costs.
j-equality-01-q3: Two immutable keys compare equal by seat code, but their hash codes are derived from different labels. What must change? => Derive both equality and hashing from the same canonical identity.
j-equality-01-q4: A SeatId record normalizes its code to upper case in the constructor. Why does that make HashMap lookups with "a1" and " A1 " work? => Both become the same canonical value, so equals and hashCode agree
j-equality-01-q5: What does map.put("Aa", 10) return if "Aa" was already mapped to 1? => 1
j-oop-02-q1: What does a valid competing request represent? => A normal business conflict with a defined outcome.
j-oop-02-q2: When is an interface worth adding? => When it captures a meaningful contract across real or test implementations.
j-oop-02-q3: The API must distinguish an unknown seat, an occupied seat and a database timeout. Which service contract preserves the distinctions? => Expose typed missing/conflict outcomes and propagate the timeout as a failure.
j-oop-02-q4: A try-with-resources body throws, and then close() also throws. What does the caller see? => The body’s exception, with the close() exception attached as suppressed
j-oop-02-q5: Why can two Strings that both print A1 compare false with ==? => == compares references, and they can be different objects with the same characters
j-generics-01-q1: When do stream intermediate operations execute? => As part of traversal driven by a terminal operation.
j-generics-01-q2: What does List<Seat> communicate? => The element type that its caller can use at compile time.
j-generics-01-q3: An ordered list contains free seats A2 and A1 in that order. What returns A2 without building a result list? => Filter by availability, then call findFirst on the ordered stream.
j-generics-01-q4: Why is List<Integer> not a subtype of List<Number>? => Because then code could add a Double to a list that must contain only Integers
j-generics-01-q5: A pipeline is seats.stream().filter(Seat::isFree).map(Seat::id).findFirst(). How many seats does it examine if the second seat is free? => Two
j-executors-01-q1: What limits overall throughput for eight database connections? => The downstream connection capacity can remain the bottleneck.
j-executors-01-q2: How can a caller see a Callable failure? => Inspect the Future and handle its execution exception.
j-executors-01-q3: Future.get times out while a booking task is waiting for a JDBC connection. What can the caller conclude? => The caller stopped waiting. The task may still continue and commit.
j-executors-01-q4: A ThreadPoolExecutor has 1 worker and a queue of 1, and both are full. What happens to a third task by default? => It is rejected with RejectedExecutionException (AbortPolicy)
j-executors-01-q5: Two threads each hold a local variable pointing to the same Seat. Can they race? => Yes, the locals are private but the Seat object they refer to is shared
l-uml-01-q1: What should the unit test assert after U2 loses? => The owner remains U1 as well as observing the false result.
l-uml-01-q2: What is a useful SOLID argument? => Connect a real reason for change to a narrowly owned responsibility.
l-uml-01-q3: A notification adapter is added. Which test best checks the responsibility split for a competing claim? => Assert a committed winner requests confirmation and a losing claim leaves owner and notifications unchanged.
l-uml-01-q4: Why use a fake repository but a real Seat in a booking unit test? => The repository is an external boundary, while Seat owns the rule under test
l-uml-01-q5: Which diagram best shows the order of calls when U2’s booking attempt fails? => Sequence diagram
j-build-01-q1: When does Spring supply a constructor dependency? => While creating the dependent bean in the application context.
j-build-01-q2: What does a successful Maven package prove? => The configured build lifecycle produced an artifact.
j-build-01-q3: A direct service unit test passes with a fake, but startup fails after adding a second repository bean. Where do you look first? => Inspect injection candidates, qualifiers and active configuration.
j-build-01-q4: Two beans implement SeatRepository and BookingService asks for one by constructor. What happens if nothing selects between them? => Startup fails with NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException until @Primary, @Qualifier or a profile resolves it
j-build-01-q5: Why is constructor injection preferred over field injection for BookingService? => Required dependencies are explicit and final, and a plain unit test can call new BookingService(fakeRepo)
b-http-01-q1: Which status fits a well-formed conflicting booking? => 409 Conflict, because the request conflicts with current ownership.
b-http-01-q2: Which request makes a read-only observation? => GET retrieves the availability representation.
b-http-01-q3: A booking API has created record B7 successfully. Which response conveys both creation and a lookup URI? => 201 Created with a Location header for /bookings/B7.
b-http-01-q4: Which HTTP methods are idempotent by definition? => GET, PUT and DELETE
b-http-01-q5: A client sends malformed JSON to POST /bookings. Which response fits? => 400 Bad Request with a stable error body
b-validation-01-q1: What error information should clients parse? => Stable documented fields or codes.
b-validation-01-q2: What validates a lawful request shape? => Boundary validation accepts it before domain conflict checks.
b-validation-01-q3: A scheduled import calls the booking service directly with a blank user ID. Which test protects the intended boundary? => Call the service directly and assert validation and no state change.
b-validation-01-q4: A batch job calls BookingService directly, bypassing the controller. Which validation still protects the seat? => Checks inside the service or domain, plus database constraints
b-validation-01-q5: Which error body is best for clients? => {"code":"SEAT_TAKEN","message":"Seat A1 is already booked"}
b-sql-01-q1: What protects a foreign-key reference? => The referenced key must exist under the schema rule.
b-sql-01-q2: What does a check constraint naturally validate? => A condition on the row values.
b-sql-01-q3: Historical rows must remain after cancellation. Which PostgreSQL rule permits rebooking and rejects two active records? => A unique index on seat_id restricted to active rows.
b-sql-01-q4: Two application instances write bookings. Which rule must live in the database to stay true? => One active booking per seat, as a unique (partial) index or constraint
b-sql-01-q5: You add a NOT NULL column to a table that already has rows. What is the safe sequence? => Add it as nullable, backfill and verify, then add NOT NULL once all writers set it
b-jdbc-01-q1: What is a Read Committed statement normally able to read? => Rows committed before that statement plus its own transaction changes.
b-jdbc-01-q2: What owns a database transaction in JDBC? => The connection executing the statements.
b-jdbc-01-q3: PostgreSQL connection B already read A1 under Repeatable Read. A commits an owner update. B reads A1 again in the same transaction. Which result is expected? => B can still see the old value from its original snapshot.
b-jdbc-01-q4: The seat update succeeds but the audit insert fails on the same connection with auto-commit off. What should the code do? => Roll back the transaction so neither change is kept
b-jdbc-01-q5: Why must a column name never be built from user input with string concatenation? => It allows SQL injection; identifiers cannot be bound, so choose them from a whitelist
b-transactions-02-q1: Where must the single-seat condition be checked? => Inside the authoritative UPDATE predicate.
b-transactions-02-q2: What can a zero-row update mean? => A missing row or a row for which the predicate failed.
b-transactions-02-q3: A transaction must reserve A1 and A2 together. Its guarded write changes A1, but A2 is already claimed. What should happen? => Roll back the transaction and return a group conflict.
b-transactions-02-q4: Which statement books A1 for U2 only if nobody owns it, in one atomic step? => UPDATE seats SET owner = 'U2' WHERE id = 'A1' AND owner IS NULL
b-transactions-02-q5: Two adjacent seats must be booked together. The first guarded update returns 1 row and the second returns 0. What should happen? => Roll back the transaction and report a group conflict
b-transactions-03-q1: What does a version check detect? => The decision was made using a stale row version.
b-transactions-03-q2: What is normally true of a selected row lock? => It is scoped to the database transaction.
b-transactions-03-q3: One transaction locks A1 then A2. A second locks A2 then A1. How do you reduce deadlock risk for the next attempts? => Acquire the seats in one stable order and handle retryable transaction failures.
b-transactions-03-q4: One very popular seat receives hundreds of concurrent booking attempts. What tends to happen with optimistic locking? => Many attempts fail on the version check and retry, adding load and tail latency
b-transactions-03-q5: How do you reduce deadlocks when a transaction locks several seats? => Lock seats in a consistent order, for example by seat ID
b-jpa-01-q1: What does flush do? => Synchronizes pending entity work with SQL execution inside the transaction.
b-jpa-01-q2: Why prefer the target DB for lock tests? => Database engines can differ in isolation and lock behavior.
b-jpa-01-q3: JPA flush emits an UPDATE, then the transaction rolls back. What should a fresh connection observe? => The prior committed row value.
b-jpa-01-q4: A list endpoint loads 50 bookings and then runs one query per booking to load each owner. What is this called? => The N+1 query problem
b-jpa-01-q5: Why can @Transactional on a test method hide a bug? => The test transaction rolls back at the end and may change visibility, so commit-time behaviour is never exercised
h-scaling-01-q1: What can coordinate two independent JVMs? => A shared authoritative database operation or equivalent coordinator.
h-scaling-01-q2: What does an availability response prove? => What one read observed at that time.
h-scaling-01-q3: Two JVMs expose the same booking API. What evidence tests shared coordination? => Send competing requests to different ports against the same database and inspect one committed owner.
h-scaling-01-q4: Two app nodes give 160 requests per second of capacity, but the database handles only 120. What does adding a third node do? => Little or nothing; the database is the bottleneck
h-scaling-01-q5: What does sticky routing (session affinity) risk hiding? => Important state kept in one instance’s memory, which is lost on failover or scale-in
h-requirements-01-q1: How should a traffic estimate be expressed? => As requests per time interval with assumptions and a separate peak.
h-requirements-01-q2: Can one seat cause trouble at low overall RPS? => Yes, if contention concentrates on that key.
h-requirements-01-q3: Peak seat-map traffic is 1,000 requests per second. At a steady 95% cache hit rate, roughly how many reach the origin if each miss fetches once? => 50 requests per second.
h-requirements-01-q4: Which is a measurable non-functional requirement? => p95 latency of POST /holds under 300 ms at 500 requests per second, measured over 10 minutes
h-requirements-01-q5: Right after a deploy, the seat-map cache is empty. What should the capacity plan assume? => Most requests miss and reach the origin until the cache fills, so origin load must be bounded, for example with request coalescing
l-invariants-02-q1: If confirmation needs now < expiry, what happens at equality? => The hold is expired for the confirmation decision.
l-invariants-02-q2: Why include the expected expiry in cleanup writes? => A stale worker should not remove a renewed hold.
l-invariants-02-q3: A hold is valid exactly while now < expiresAt. Confirmation arrives exactly at expiresAt and cleanup has not run. What should the confirmation do? => Reject as expired in the authoritative transition.
l-invariants-02-q4: Cleanup runs every 5 minutes. A hold expired 2 minutes ago and its row still says HELD. Another user tries to claim the seat. What should happen? => Allow the claim if the guarded write treats the expired hold as reclaimable
l-invariants-02-q5: Why should expiry tests use a controllable clock? => It lets the test set the exact time, so boundary cases like now = expiresAt are deterministic
b-http-02-q1: Where should the replay record and effect commit? => Together where the same database can enforce atomicity.
b-http-02-q2: What should happen when the key matches and the payload does not? => Reject the reuse according to the contract.
b-http-02-q3: Booking committed but the response was lost. A retry uses the same key and payload inside the retention window. What result demonstrates the contract? => Return the stored result and retain one booking effect.
b-http-02-q4: Which fields should scope an idempotency record? => Authenticated caller, operation and key, plus a hash of the normalized request
b-http-02-q5: A client times out and retries with a new idempotency key. What can happen? => A second booking may be created if the first one committed
h-databases-01-q1: What does EXPLAIN ANALYZE do? => It executes the statement and includes actual observations.
h-databases-01-q2: Is an asynchronous replica a safe authority for a new booking? => Its reads may lag, so the write must use the enforcing path.
h-databases-01-q3: A PostgreSQL index is unused for a tiny table, with matching rows spread across most pages. What is the best next step? => Compare actual plans using representative data sizes and selectivity.
h-databases-01-q4: A query filters by event_id and orders by seat_no. Which index fits best? => (event_id, seat_no)
h-databases-01-q5: A user books a seat and immediately reloads “My bookings”, which reads from a lagging replica. What fixes the empty page? => Route that user’s reads to the primary for a short time after a write, or read with a known commit position
b-caching-01-q1: Where is the booking decision made if the cache looks free? => In the authoritative booking operation.
b-caching-01-q2: When should ordinary invalidation run? => After commit for the write whose result it reflects.
b-caching-01-q3: A reader fetches “available.” The writer commits, invalidates, and then the reader refills the cache with its old result. What must still hold? => A new booking attempt reaches the database guard and cannot create a second owner.
b-caching-01-q4: A popular seat map key expires and 500 requests miss at once. What reduces the load on the database? => Request coalescing so one request refills the key while the others wait
b-caching-01-q5: Which eviction policy keeps a popular key during a one-off scan of many cold keys? => LFU, because the popular key has a high use count
b-messaging-01-q1: What ordering does Kafka provide? => Ordering within a partition.
b-messaging-01-q2: What can cause measurable redelivery? => Completing a side effect and dying before committing consumer progress.
b-messaging-01-q3: A consumer commits a database effect, then crashes before acknowledging the event. What protects against applying it twice? => An event ID stored transactionally with that effect.
b-messaging-01-q4: A topic has 4 partitions and a consumer group has 6 consumers. What happens? => 4 consumers get one partition each and 2 stay idle
b-messaging-01-q5: Which design deduplicates a booking-confirmed event safely? => Insert the event ID into a table with a unique constraint in the same transaction as the effect
h-loadbalance-01-q1: What should a load-test result include? => The workload shape, rate, duration, errors and sample count.
h-loadbalance-01-q2: What does a load balancer solve? => How requests reach service instances.
h-loadbalance-01-q3: Increasing offered load raises throughput and p95. Which measurement best checks whether database admission is driving the change? => Per-request connection acquisition wait and pool saturation under the same traffic mix.
h-loadbalance-01-q4: The mean latency is 40 ms but users complain. What should you check first? => Tail percentiles such as p95 and p99 for the affected endpoint
h-loadbalance-01-q5: One instance has slow database access. Which balancer feature helps most? => Least-outstanding-requests routing with outlier detection
h-consistency-01-q1: What follows from a write timeout? => The caller may not know whether the server committed.
h-consistency-01-q2: What is an appropriate source for a strict booking confirmation? => An authoritative enforcing path.
h-consistency-01-q3: Region B can serve a cached map but cannot reach the booking authority. What behavior preserves unique ownership? => Permit the approved stale view and fail claims that cannot be authorized.
h-consistency-01-q4: Three services each retry 3 times. A request at the top fails at the bottom. Up to how many bottom-layer calls can result? => 27
h-consistency-01-q5: Under PACELC, what choice remains when there is no partition? => Between latency and consistency
d-complexity-01-q1: What does n stand for in the scan? => The number of input observations under the stated model.
d-complexity-01-q2: What enables O(1) range sum after preprocessing? => Subtract two prefix sums.
d-complexity-01-q3: With prefix[0]=0 and prefix[i+1]=prefix[i]+a[i], what computes the sum of a[l..r) after preprocessing? => prefix[r] − prefix[l].
d-complexity-01-q4: A method makes n HashSet insertions, and each ID is a string of up to m characters. What is a fair expected time bound? => O(n·m)
d-complexity-01-q5: What is the peak stack depth of naive recursive Fibonacci F(n)? => O(n)
d-pointers-01-q1: Why is a two-pointer scan often linear? => Each monotone boundary crosses the input at most once.
d-pointers-01-q2: What happens to the left edge after seeing an old duplicate outside the current span? => It should not move backward.
d-pointers-01-q3: In a,b,b,a, left is 2 before processing the final a. Its previous index is 0. What is left after processing it? => 2.
d-pointers-01-q4: Why does a shrink-when-too-large sliding window fail when the array contains negative numbers? => The window sum is no longer monotone, so a discarded window might have led to a valid answer
d-pointers-01-q5: In a sorted array, a[left] + a[right] is smaller than the target. Which move is safe? => left++
d-sort-01-q1: What helps preserve merge sort stability on ties? => Choose the left-side item first.
d-sort-01-q2: Which references must be kept before reversing a link? => The next unprocessed node and the reversed prefix.
d-sort-01-q3: You are reversing A→B→C and have current=B, previous=A. What must you save before setting B.next to A? => The original B.next, which points to C.
d-sort-01-q4: Booking requests must be sorted by priority while keeping arrival order for equal priorities. Which Java call does that? => list.sort(Comparator.comparingInt(Req::priority)), because object sorting is stable
d-sort-01-q5: Which input does a stack-based validator report as unclosed? => "(()"
d-lru-02-q1: What does a successful get change? => The node moves to most-recently used.
d-lru-02-q2: Where must eviction remove the key? => From both the map and the linked list.
d-lru-02-q3: A capacity-two LRU runs put(A), put(B), get(A), put(C). Which key should be removed? => B.
d-lru-02-q4: Why must get on an LRU cache be inside the same lock as put? => Because a hit moves the entry in the recency order, which is shared state
d-lru-02-q5: Which Java setup gives LRU eviction in a few lines? => LinkedHashMap with accessOrder = true and removeEldestEntry returning size() > capacity
d-recursion-01-q1: What does inorder produce for a valid BST? => Key order according to the BST’s ordering rule.
d-recursion-01-q2: What heap entry must be efficiently replaceable for k smallest? => The largest currently retained value.
d-recursion-01-q3: To keep the smallest three values from a stream, your retained set is 2, 5 and 8, and the next is 4. What should happen? => Replace 8 with 4 by removing the max-heap root.
d-recursion-01-q4: A recursive traversal of a BST built by inserting 1, 2, 3, …, 1,000,000 in order throws StackOverflowError. Why? => Sorted inserts make the tree a chain of height n, so the recursion is n calls deep
d-recursion-01-q5: What is the time and space cost of keeping the k nearest items from a stream of n with a bounded heap? => O(n log k) time, O(k) space
d-graphs-01-q1: What guarantee holds for BFS shortest path? => Fewest edges in an unweighted graph.
d-graphs-01-q2: When should a BFS vertex normally be marked discovered? => When it is enqueued.
d-graphs-01-q3: S→T costs 5. S→A and A→T each cost 1. Which paths minimize hops and total weight? => S→T minimizes hops. S→A→T minimizes weight.
d-graphs-01-q4: An undirected graph has 7 vertices and edges 0–1, 1–2 and 3–4. How many connected components does it have? => 4
d-graphs-01-q5: During a DFS of a directed graph, you reach a vertex that is grey (still on the current path). What does that mean? => There is a cycle
d-greedy-01-q1: Does earliest finish maximize arbitrary total value? => No, weighted intervals can require a recurrence.
d-greedy-01-q2: What does including a weighted interval add? => Its weight plus the optimum for its compatible predecessor.
d-greedy-01-q3: Intervals [0,2), [2,4) and [0,4) have values 1, 1 and 10. What is the maximum total value without overlap? => 10.
d-greedy-01-q4: Bookings must leave a 10-minute reset. Booking P is [0, 60). Which of these can follow P directly? => A booking starting at 70
d-greedy-01-q5: What makes weighted interval scheduling O(n log n) rather than O(n²)? => Finding each compatible predecessor p(i) by binary search over jobs sorted by end time
b-security-01-q1: What does authentication establish? => The caller’s identity from trusted credentials.
b-security-01-q2: What should happen if scope allows reading and ownership rejects? => The request remains forbidden under the resource policy.
b-security-01-q3: A valid access token has booking:read. The caller is assigned venue A and requests a booking in venue B. What should the service do? => Deny access under the resource-level policy and avoid returning booking details.
b-security-01-q4: Why might an API return 404 rather than 403 when a signed-in user requests someone else’s booking? => It makes foreign and missing IDs look the same, so callers cannot probe which bookings exist
b-security-01-q5: Which test would catch a handler that checks login but not ownership? => A second signed-in user requests the owner’s booking and is refused
b-deployment-01-q1: Which signal gates traffic admission? => Readiness, which reports whether this instance can take traffic.
b-deployment-01-q2: What should stay outside the container image? => Environment-specific credentials and settings.
b-deployment-01-q3: A shared DB is down for 30 seconds. An instance remains responsive but cannot handle booking traffic. Which probes fit? => Readiness fails for booking traffic and liveness remains healthy if the process can recover.
b-deployment-01-q4: Which metric label is safe for a booking API? => The route template /events/{id}/bookings
b-deployment-01-q5: Every replica includes the shared database in its liveness probe. The database is down for 30 seconds. What happens? => All replicas fail liveness and are restarted together, making the outage longer
ai-foundations-02-q1: What updates model weights? => Training, which adjusts model parameters using data.
ai-foundations-02-q2: What makes comparison more reliable? => The same representative inputs, constraints and output checks.
ai-foundations-02-q3: Two models give wrong answers without policy text and both succeed when given the same correct passage. What should you diagnose first? => Whether retrieval reliably includes the passage for that question.
ai-foundations-02-q4: The refund policy changed yesterday. How can the assistant answer with the new rule? => Supply the current policy passage in the context at request time
ai-foundations-02-q5: Two model options give the same grounded results on the fixtures. One has p95 400 ms and a tenth of the cost. What should you choose? => The faster, cheaper one, while it meets the quality bar on the same fixtures
ai-prompting-01-q1: What does structured output mainly constrain? => Fields and types of the generated result.
ai-prompting-01-q2: What is a safe policy response after failed evidence validation? => Return the defined deterministic fallback.
ai-prompting-01-q3: A response parses and cites P1. P1 says 48 hours and the response says 24. What should happen? => Reject the unsupported claim and use the defined fallback.
ai-prompting-01-q4: A reply has "answerable": "true" (a string) instead of a boolean. Which stage rejects it? => The shape (schema) check, as malformed
ai-prompting-01-q5: Where should the user’s question go in the prompt? => Into the user message, inside delimiters, with < and > escaped
ai-model-api-01-q1: Who owns booking correctness? => The booking domain and authoritative persistence.
ai-model-api-01-q2: What does a fixture adapter improve? => Repeatability of tests for output and failure handling.
ai-model-api-01-q3: A provider moves its generated text into a different JSON field. Which test gives the clearest signal? => An adapter contract test using a response fixture with the changed wire shape.
ai-model-api-01-q4: A provider responds after 5 seconds and the help budget is 2 seconds. What should the user see? => A short fallback message with links to the policy pages, returned within the budget
ai-model-api-01-q5: Where should the model API key be stored? => In a secret store or environment variable injected at runtime
ai-embeddings-01-q1: Why use the same embedding space? => Queries and documents need comparable vector representations.
ai-embeddings-01-q2: When is lexical matching helpful? => For known exact codes and phrases.
ai-embeddings-01-q3: A valid policy code misses vector search. There is also a semantically close document from an unauthorized venue. Which change is appropriate? => Add exact code matching and apply venue and version filters to all candidate paths.
ai-embeddings-01-q4: Your vector query is filtered by venue, but the keyword query is not. What can go wrong? => A passage from another venue can enter the merged results through the keyword path
ai-embeddings-01-q5: Your team switches to a new embedding model. What must happen to the stored passages? => Re-embed them with the new model, ideally into a new index, and evaluate before switching
ai-rag-01-q1: What is supplied to a RAG generator? => Evidence retrieved for the current request.
ai-rag-01-q2: What should no supporting evidence trigger? => The documented insufficient-evidence fallback.
ai-rag-01-q3: Retrieval contains the current authorized clause, but the answer introduces an exception absent from it. What failed? => Claim grounding or its validation, even though retrieval found the passage.
ai-rag-01-q4: In RagPipeline.java the answer cites P2 but says 24 hours, while P2 says 48 hours. What does the pipeline return? => A validation fallback: the claim is not in the cited text
ai-rag-01-q5: Both the current policy (v3) and an outdated one (v2) match the question. Where should the outdated one be removed? => In retrieval, by filtering on the current flag or effective date before ranking
ai-evaluation-01-q1: What does retrieval hit@k measure on a labeled answerable question set? => The fraction of questions with at least one relevant passage in the top k results.
ai-evaluation-01-q2: What supports an evaluation regression claim? => The same fixtures and evaluation rules across versions.
ai-evaluation-01-q3: A revision sends fewer bad answers, but also refuses more questions with good evidence. What should the evaluation report? => Grounded correctness and refusal rates separately for answerable and unanswerable cases.
ai-evaluation-01-q4: Twenty help calls have a mean latency of 980 ms, but the 19th and 20th sorted values are 2,000 ms. What should you report? => p50 and p95 with the timeout count, because the mean hides the slow tail
ai-evaluation-01-q5: v2 is 100% grounded on the answers it gives but refuses 3 of 4 answerable questions. What is the right conclusion? => It is a trade-off: report false refusals next to grounded correctness and decide with the product owner
ai-tools-01-q1: What does a model tool proposal authorize? => Nothing by itself; the application must validate and authorize it.
